context:
Goal: You can always see what a rate said before it was corrected.
Problem (risk): A q_max rule says a saved rate is never changed: a fix keeps the old row and adds a new one. But the code changes saved rates directly in 7 places, and nothing warns when someone adds an 8th.
Based on (read): 7 update sites, approvalLedger.ts:910, observationStore.ts:464 and 5 more (main 5bbf10e).
Based on (ruling): an-award-files-its-lines-as-rates (2026-10-01) already lets one of them change in place.
Departs from: the rule says never change a saved rate, and the code changes it in 7 places — the rule names the allowed changes, and a check flags any new one.

lastAnswer.note: this is so hard to understand indont know how to decide because the queetion isnt intuitive for me to understand

options.gain: The rule tells the truth, and any new change is caught.
options.how: The rule lists the 7 allowed changes; a check flags any new place that changes a saved rate.
options.label: Allow the known changes, flag new ones
options.lose: A few saved rates can still change without a trace of the old value.

options.how: Rewrite the 7 places to keep the old row and add a new one.
options.label: Never change a saved rate
options.lose: 7 places in the code must be rewritten, which can put stored rates at risk.

title: q_max: When a saved rate is wrong, may the code change it in place?
why: It makes the rule match the code and catches any new change.
